title: Fallback Finesse Flashcards v0.1
content:
Purpose:
Quick, bite-sized actionable flashcards for SEs and field ops to run through common inference production failure modes during pilots and early production. Not a replacement for runbooks; intended as 30-90s decision aides in calls or war-room handoffs.

How to use this doc (notes to self):
- Print a deck of 2-3 cards for an SE before a pilot kickoff.
- Trainer runs 10-min roleplay using 3 vignettes.
- Each card = crisis phrase, immediate stop-gap, fallback script to read verbatim, metrics to collect, next-step play.
- Keep language prescriptive and minimal; avoid deep infra detail. Link to runbooks for escalation.

Slide 1: One-line framing (speaker note)
- "When latency, cost, or quality surprise you in a demo/pilot, run these three moves first."
- 30s intro: objective is to buy time, protect user experience, and gather triage signals.

CARD A: Latency spike during demo
- Trigger: median p50 latency >3x baseline or p95 > 2s over SLO during a live demo or onboarding test.
- Immediate stop-gap (30s): Switch to lower-latency model variant & reduce max_tokens to 50 for interactive demos. Trigger: use routing policy 'fast-fallback' in console.
- Verbatim fallback script (read to customer): "We're seeing increased latency; I'm switching the session to a faster model variant to keep the experience responsive. We'll capture logs and follow up with the optimized settings later."
- Quick signals to capture: request_ids (last 5), p50/p95, model_version, region, batch size, KV cache hit rate.
- Post-action: create JIRA card tagging infra with 'latency-spike', attach request traces and policy change timestamp.
- Escalate if persists >10 minutes or impacts >20% of requests.
- Demo checklist: test 1x generate, confirm streaming enabled, confirm client-side idle timeout <=2s.

CARD B: Token cost runaway on pilot batch
- Trigger: cost per 1k tokens > expected by +40% over 24h or unexpected spike after dataset change.
- Immediate stop-gap (30s): Enable n-best=1, reduce max_tokens, and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. Consider applying per-route quotas.
- Verbatim fallback script: "We're seeing token consumption higher than expected. I'll temporarily tighten generation params and enable caching so the pilot stays within budget while we investigate."
- Signals: tokens_in/out, sampling params (temperature/top_p), prompt length, cache key hit rate, route_id.
- Post-action: Run prompt audit (top 10 longest prompts) and link to product eval ticket if this is due to prompt drift.
- Escalate to product if reduction changes output quality beyond acceptance criteria.

CARD C: Generation quality regression (sudden hallucinations / truncated outputs)
- Trigger: >3 customer-reported quality failures in 24 hours or automated eval failing new prompts by >15% relative.
- Immediate stop-gap (30s): Roll back to previous model version pinned in canary, or route to 'quality-optimized' profile. Enable deterministic sampling (temperature 0) for critical responses.
- Verbatim fallback script: "We have a quality regression on this model version. I'm routing your requests to the previously pinned model version until we verify fixes. We'll keep you posted on any changes."
- Signals: eval pass/fail history, prompting changes, model commit id, token truncation logs, output length.
- Post-action: Create an eval-run and attach failing prompts; triage with applied-ml. Add label 'regression' + model_version.

CARD D: Private deployment networking flake (VPC egress / peering intermittent)
- Trigger: failed handshakes from private control plane, periodic 502/504 errors only from private routes.
- Immediate stop-gap (30s): Failover to hosted console route for control plane operations, flag requests for retry with exponential backoff, and temporarily pause non-essential background jobs.
- Verbatim fallback script: "We're seeing intermittent network issues in the private network. We'll failover control operations to our hosted console and pause heavy background jobs while the network stabilizes."
- Signals: control-plane health checks, BGP/peering alerts, route table changes, cloud provider incident id.
- Post-action: Engage private-deployments SRE, open support ticket with customer cloud provider, share trace IDs.

CARD E: Dedicated capacity throttle / quota exhaustion during ramp
- Trigger: queued requests increasing, allocation errors, or autoscaler hitting cap.
- Immediate stop-gap (30s): Enable short-term burst capacity if available, or route lowest-priority traffic to a cheaper model-variant. Notify account owner and enable maintenance window for scaling test.
- Verbatim fallback script: "We've hit a capacity limit during this ramp. We'll temporarily redirect lower-priority traffic and request burst capacity so your high-priority flows remain healthy while we scale."
- Signals: instance utilization, queue depth, autoscaler events, reservation utilization.
- Post-action: Submit capacity increase request, plan a controlled ramp test with load profile, recommend committed reserved capacity for steady-state.

CARD F: Integrator API contract mismatch (schema / function-calling errors)
- Trigger: repeated function call failures, 400/422 errors from clients after a recent change.
- Immediate stop-gap (30s): Revert schema change or enable backward-compatible route alias; set feature flag to legacy function-calling mode.
- Verbatim fallback script: "Looks like a schema mismatch from a recent change. I'm switching your integration to the legacy call shape while we coordinate a proper migration."
- Signals: client_error_codes, last-deploy-by, payload diffs, function-calling logs.
- Post-action: Sync with integrator, update API spec, schedule migration window.

Playbook appendices (short links for the SE):
- 1-page runbook link (internal): CONFLUENCE-12345://fallback-runbooks (add to deck)
- Fast trace gathering checklist: how-to get request IDs, KV cache dumps, console trace link patterns.
- Escalation matrix: who to pager for infra, applied-ml, private-deployments, and account success.

Trainer notes and suggested roleplays:
- 10-min drill: SE + SRE + customer actor. Scenario: latency spike during a pilot demo. Run 3 cycles; time the fallbacks and confirm logs collected.
- Scoring rubric: time-to-first-fallback, customer-facing phrasing clarity, evidence attached in Jira, escalation decisions correct.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Should we default to a single, canonical 'fast-fallback' route id with a pinned model mapping? (Arjun to prototype)
- Determine exact burst capacity SLAs and how to surface to sales during contract negotiation. (SRE + finance)
- Add one-liners for commercial teams about cost impact of each fallback option (rough $/1k tokens delta).

Quick snippets for Slack / customer message templates (copy-paste friendly):
- Latency: "We're seeing slower responses; switching to a faster model variant now and capturing traces. Expect normal UX in <5 mins."
- Cost: "We've applied tighter generation limits to keep this pilot within the budgeted token spend; we'll follow up with optimization suggestions."
- Quality: "Routing to previous model version while we investigate a regression. Your results should be consistent during the investigation."

Version history (meta):
- v0.1 2026-02-15 initial draft (this file).
- v0.2 planned: add cost deltas, add quick link cards for legal/contract asks, finalize one-liners.

Notes to reviewers: please give feedback on: clarity of the fallbacks, any missing signals to capture automatically, and whether the customer-facing scripts are conservative enough.
